result:
**Verdict: approve.** I found no concrete VM bug in the follow-up. It removes the remaining source uncertainty: the old extra tick after swap/jump was wrong, and dropping it matches native behaviour. One unenforced contract point is noted under limitations. I only read source; I did not run the tests, so the "14 Cut tests/TSC pass" claim comes from you.

```json
{
  "verdict": "approve",
  "scope": "FOLLOWUP.diff only, plus the source functions needed to check it. No editing or execution.",
  "findings": [],
  "phaseProof": {
    "dispatchTick": "Tick N: Task_RunScripts (script_manager.c:114-121) calls RunScriptCommand. The swap command (scrcmd_c.c:4436-4452 -> map_object_swap_positions.c:33-35) and the jump command (scrcmd_c.c:4924-4928 -> follow_mon_interaction.c:1457-1463) call TaskManager_Call, which makes the child the active task (task.c:41-47), and then return TRUE. That breaks the bytecode loop (script.c:83-84), and Task_RunScripts returns FALSE (script_manager.c:144). The while loop in FieldSystem_RunTaskFrame (task.c:55) therefore stops, so the child does not run in tick N.",
    "childTicks": "From tick N+1 the child is the active task and runs once per frame. Task_FollowMonJumpOnSpot (follow_mon_interaction.c:1466-1503) returns TRUE only in state 4.",
    "completionTick": "Tick K: the child returns TRUE. task.c:56-62 frees it, restores prev (the script task), and the while condition calls Task_RunScripts again in the same tick K. Bytecode resumes in mode BYTECODE.",
    "sameTickChain": "After the swap: GetPartyLeadAlive, GetPartyMonSpecies, Call _025B, FollowMonAddMood 20 and FirstAliveMonHasType all return FALSE (scrcmd_party.c:309-313, scrcmd_c.c:4907-4922), so mood+20 lands on the swap-completion tick. The script then dispatches JumpOnSpot 2 (Grass/Chikorita) and stops. When the jump child completes, FollowMonAddMood 1, Return and PlayCry (scrcmd_sound.c:115-120 returns FALSE) all run in that tick, then WaitCry suspends. This matches the test expectations [[4,20],[7,1]] and cry@7.",
    "resetTick": "ScrCmd_FollowMonResetMovement (scrcmd_c.c:4570-4576) returns TRUE without calling TaskManager_Call, so the script task returns FALSE and resumes on the next frame. The explicit waitFrames(1) and the assertion that cutIn comes one tick after the reset are correct.",
    "diglettSkip": "When the species is Diglett/Dugtrio, FollowMon_JumpOnSpot creates no child, but the command still returns TRUE. Bytecode resumes on tick N+1, so the documented requirement that the port wait one dispatch tick is source-correct.",
    "deltaCorrectness": "awaitedField is used only by reset (script.ts:162), swap (:217) and jump (:220). Removing the waitFrames(1) that only applied to Cut and re-adding it only for reset gives exactly the native phases. Non-Cut paths are unchanged, because the removed wait was already limited to Cut."
  },
  "hostObligations": [
    "The swap/jump port Promise must resolve on the same tick the native child returns TRUE. The child first runs on the frame after dispatch, so a child that runs k frames resolves at dispatch + k. That means at least 1 tick; a port that resolves synchronously or in a microtask would be one frame early.",
    "The Diglett/Dugtrio skip must resolve exactly 1 dispatch tick later. The VM cannot infer the registered native follower species from its own actor, so it cannot enforce this.",
    "Use a real TaskManager-equivalent phase: resolve at the child's completion/resource-release point, not after an extra host frame.",
    "Honour the abort/cancel signals and the field-change rejection. These are unchanged from before."
  ],
  "vmDefects": [],
  "optionalHardening": "The VM could reject or warn when a swap/jump port resolves on the dispatch tick (fewer than 1 frame). Native code never completes on that tick, including the Diglett skip. Not required by the contract as written.",
  "limitations": [
    "Assumes FieldSystem_RunTaskFrame is called once per frame (the parent main integration was out of scope).",
    "The new test checks the native task.c loop with a regex and models the children with timed fakes (4 and 3 ticks). It does not check real movement-script durations.",
    "Did not run the tests or TSC (read-only)."
  ]
}
```
